cards.explanation: The answer is: do not fear what they fear. The LORD tells Isaiah, “Do not fear what they fear; do not live in dread.” (Isaiah 8:12) Panic spreads faster than a yawn in a meeting, friends, so this was a good thing to hear. Isaiah doesn't have to catch it.

The answer is the LORD of Hosts. The LORD says, “The LORD of Hosts is the One you shall regard as holy. Only He should be feared; only He should be dreaded.” (Isaiah 8:13) Notice the word “only,” friends. That leaves no room for a second name on the list.

The answer is True. The LORD will be a sanctuary, but to both houses of Israel He will be “…a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense…” (Isaiah 8:14). It's one verse with two sides, bakers, and both halves are in there.

The answer is that Isaiah will wait for the LORD and trust Him. He says, “I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding His face from the house of Jacob. I will put my trust in Him.” (Isaiah 8:17) Waiting isn't flashy, friends. I spent plenty of time waiting myself, so I know it's some of the hardest work there is.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, “Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me as signs and symbols in Israel from the LORD of Hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.” (Isaiah 8:18) I think any father would stand a little taller saying that. I know I would.

The answer is “God.” Isaiah asks, “…shouldn’t a people consult their God instead?” (Isaiah 8:19) It's a question with its answer built in, friends. The mediums and spiritists are the ones who whisper and mutter, and Isaiah points the people to their God instead.

The answer is “dead.” Isaiah asks, “Why consult the dead on behalf of the living?” (Isaiah 8:19) That question comes right after he talks about mediums and spiritists. The dead are the ones being consulted, and the living are the ones it's for.

The answer is that they curse their king and their God. Isaiah says, “When they are famished, they will become enraged; and looking upward, they will curse their king and their God.” (Isaiah 8:21) I think it's a heavy one, friends. It's a hard picture of people at the end of themselves.

The answer is False. When the people look to the earth, Isaiah says they “…see only distress and darkness and the gloom of anguish.” (Isaiah 8:22) Then they're “…driven into utter darkness.” No dawn there, bakers, which makes the next chapter hit even harder.

The answer is Zebulun and Naphtali. Isaiah says, “In the past He humbled the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future He will honor the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations…” (Isaiah 9:1) Humbled before, honored after. That's quite a turn, friends.

The answer is “light.” Isaiah says, “The people walking in darkness have seen a great light; on those living in the land of the shadow of death, a light has dawned.” (Isaiah 9:2) After the gloom at the end of chapter 8, this is the turn, bakers. Light is the whole point.

The answer is harvest time. Isaiah says, “The people rejoice before You as they rejoice at harvest time, as men rejoice in dividing the plunder.” (Isaiah 9:3) Their joy is compared to the joy of harvest time, and also to the joy of men dividing the plunder. Harvest time is the picture the question asks about, friends.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, “For as in the day of Midian You have shattered the yoke of their burden, the bar across their shoulders, and the rod of their oppressor.” (Isaiah 9:4) Three things get shattered: the yoke, the bar and the rod. That's a lot of breaking in one verse, friends.

The answer is that they will be burned as fuel for the fire. Isaiah says, “For every trampling boot of battle and every garment rolled in blood will be burned as fuel for the fire.” (Isaiah 9:5) Nobody is putting those boots in the closet to use again, bakers. They're going up in flames.

The answer is the child's shoulders. Isaiah says, “…the government will be upon His shoulders.” (Isaiah 9:6) Look at the shoulders in these two verses, friends. The bar across the people's shoulders gets shattered (Isaiah 9:4), and then the government rests on the child's shoulders.

The answer is True. Isaiah says, “Of the increase of His government and peace there will be no end.” (Isaiah 9:7) It keeps growing and there's no end to it, friends. Most things I bake end when somebody grabs the last cookie.

The answer is David. Isaiah says, “He will reign on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish and sustain it with justice and righteousness from that time and forevermore.” (Isaiah 9:7) The throne is David's, friends. The “He” is the one called Wonderful Counselor in the verse before (Isaiah 9:6).

The answer is False. Isaiah doesn't say the people's own strength accomplishes this. The last line says, “The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.” (Isaiah 9:7) The people don't have to pull it off in their own strength, friends. The LORD's zeal does it.
